data.title: Nepal: Glacial collapse leaves 3,000 missing
data.description: Rescue and relief efforts in Nepal and Tibet have been hampered this Sunday by heavy rain and rising river levels. The latest figures following Wednesday’s flash floods put the death toll at 750, while more than 3,000 people remain missing. Nepal’s disaster authorities are urging rescue teams to “exercise caution”, warning that bad weather, swollen rivers and the threat of further flooding could hamper operations. Shazab Wahlah reports from the town of Bidur.

data.title: Gunman kills one at Swiss rave party
data.description: A large-scale police operation is underway in Switzerland after a shooting at a rave in the town of Aarau, 46 kilometres west of Zurich, left one person dead and five others injured. Police are appealing to potential witnesses who may have photos or videos of the incident to come forward and share them with investigators. France 24 correspondent John Zarocostas reports from Zurich.

data.title: French Presidential campaign heats up
data.description: There are just eight months to go before France’s presidential election, with the first round scheduled for April 18. The campaign is slowly heating up, with several political gatherings taking place this weekend. The Socialist Party wrapped up a two-day gathering on Saturday with a speech from party leader Olivier Faure, who has yet to officially announce his candidacy. Meanwhile, far-right figure Jordan Bardella made a campaign stop at a fair in the Champagne region. This comes after a first debate earlier this week between seven of the leading candidates, organised by business leaders. For an analysis of the current state of the race, we’re joined by Renaud Foucart, a Senior Lecturer in Economics at Lancaster University and one of our go-to analysts on French politics.

data.title: AI vaginas, customisable personalities and fake bruises: the sex doll market is booming. Does it matter how the dolls are treated?
data.description: As the sex doll industry grows and AI changes the products available, what does it mean to engage in any kind of relationship with a woman-shaped thing? Two weeks ago, two distressed citizens stumbled across what they assumed was the mangled corpse of a woman, stuffed into a suitcase in a small town about three hours south of Sydney. They called the local police, who in turn issued a statement that a body in a suitcase had been found. The wider public waited sombrely for Australia’s tally of dead women to tick up by one. But instead, a day later, after forensic analysis, it was determined that the woman in question wasn’t a woman at all. The “body” was that of a sex doll, marked with fake bruises , left to rot on a lonely dirt road. In Australia, as in the UK and some other European countries, it is not illegal to own a sex doll unless it resembles a child. Given the doll’s seemingly mature presentation, police investigations were called off. Continue reading...

data.title: The moment I knew: I’d never had romantic feelings for a man – then he touched my hand and it felt electric
data.description: As a widower and a newly single father of three, Jim Rogers was struggling. Then on a poolside holiday, he sat next to Tyler – and his life changed Find more stories from the moment I knew series In the mid 90s, I was in the prime of my life. I was in my early 30s, married to my soul mate, Lorna, with three kids under three. We’d emigrated from our small town in Worcestershire in the UK to Perth, and life was wonderful. Then Lorna was diagnosed with melanoma. We returned to England and less than a year later she was gone. It was completely unbelievable, as though someone had just come along and smashed my life into a million pieces. The following months were a blur: I was a grief-stricken widower and newly single parent struggling to keep the kids’ life on track and my own head above water. As time went on, it was obvious I wasn’t doing well and my parents insisted on treating me to a holiday in the sun. I didn’t want to go. Continue reading...

data.title: Messina mystery: theft of Renaissance art from Sicilian museum leaves investigators baffled
data.description: How did thieves pull off robbery of Antonello da Messina’s 15th-century masterpiece – and why did they leave part of it behind? At about 8.47pm on the evening of 15 August, while tens of thousands of worshippers filled the streets of central Messina for a religious festival, at least two men cut through the fencing surrounding the regional museum, located a few miles to the north on the outskirts of the Sicilian harbour city. Capitalising on the fact that the streets around the museum were unusually quiet, the men forced open a side door with a crowbar, gaining direct access to a display case containing the five surviving panels of the Renaissance master Antonello da Messina’s polyptych Polittico di San Gregorio , his most important work, and a small double-sided painting. Undisturbed, they removed the works from the building and fled. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘I was miserable for a lot of this century’: Stewart Lee on divorce, his adoption and the twisted children’s poem that explains his life
data.description: After a rocky few decades, the standup is nearing 60 – and finding contentment at last. But what does his grotesque retelling of The Owl and the Pussy-cat tell us about his inability to connect with people? Stewart Lee is somewhat fretfully tidying his kitchen. Nothing is exactly where he left it two months ago to go on tour. Plus, he says, “I’ve come back with a load of records that need to be alphabetised, and that’s really stressing me out.” His house is miles from minimalist – posters everywhere, for spaghetti westerns, avant-garde Welsh harpists, the Fall (who he said in an interview in 2005 were the love of his life ) – but if anything was an inch out of place, he’d notice. He puts things away with theatrical flourish, like a guy doing an impression of a guy who needs things just-so, for the comic effect of how absolutely impossible that guy would be, but at the same time, it’s funny because it’s true. In the show he’s been away for, Stewart Lee vs the Man-Wulf, he – a 58-year-old lefty – enters into breakneck dialectic with toxic masculinity in werewolf form (age unknown). “Things have got worse in the 18 months I’ve been doing it,” he says. “I need to really amp the werewolf up. He would be much more explicitly racist and homophobic and transphobic now. But you don’t want people to be really upset in the room.” It feels quite a 2026 dilemma, being unable to even satirise the right without causing the distress it lives for. Continue reading...

While our interactions there are limited, we also attend a weekly non-school activity . What began as casual conversation has become much more significant in my mind. I find myself looking forward to seeing them, thinking about our conversations later, and wondering what might have been if we ’d met in different circumstances. They are married with children too. Nothing inappropriate has happened, and neither of us has acknowledged any romantic feelings. However, I cannot shake the sense that there may be a mutual connection. Continue reading...

data.title: Big tech goes to Hollywood: is Silicon Valley ready for a silver-screen reckoning?
data.description: Its moguls are ripe subjects for drama, and there is huge anticipation for forthcoming features The Social Reckoning and Artificial. But other projects have failed as the film industry is increasingly colonised by IT empires • Tom Cruise, Olivia Colman and the return of Rocky: the best films of autumn 2026 • See all of our unmissable autumn arts recommendations here ‘I know there are easier enemies to make,” tech reporter Jeremy Allen White tells his colleague in a recent trailer for The Social Reckoning. “The mafia would be an easier enemy to make,” comes the reply. They’re talking about Mark Zuckerberg’s Meta, but they might as well be discussing big tech as a whole. As The Social Reckoning promises to underline, it’s become clear that these people are not on our side – “us” being the whole of humanity except billionaire tech overlords and their mates. But for an industry that loves a clear-cut baddie, Hollywood has barely landed a blow on the tech industry. Now it finds itself in mortal danger of being absorbed by it. Is it too late to fight back? The Social Reckoning’s predecessor, The Social Network, showed how this kind of thing is done. It was pacy, buzzy and full of weirder-than-life characters – not least the young Zuckerberg, portrayed by Jesse Eisenberg as an obnoxiously smart mogul-in-the-making, whose mission to connect the world stood in stark contrast to his own social deficiencies. Directed by David Fincher and co-written by Aaron Sorkin, it was also a commercial and critical hit, winning three Oscars. But a big part of what made The Social Network work, and makes its sequel such a threat, is that it was about the actual, real-world Silicon Valley, which is where a lot of recent entertainment has gone wrong. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘That’s what saved me’: Darren Raymond and Mark Rylance on the prison drama workshop that brought them together
data.description: A masterclass led by the actor helped set Raymond on a new path. Now the head of a theatre company, he has coaxed his friend back to the stage for a show to encourage young people to fall in love with performing Darren Raymond doesn’t remember having any significant interest in acting when he was growing up. And when he met Mark Rylance for the first time, on Christmas Eve 2004, he had never heard of the multi-award winning actor. These days, things are very different: Raymond is the artistic director of Intermission Youth, the London-based arts charity and theatre, and is directing his friend Rylance in the lead role of Tartuffe (Remixed), Raymond’s adaptation of the Molière play, which opens at London’s Marylebone theatre this week. It’s fair to say neither could have anticipated they’d still be in touch this long after their initial meeting. “Unlikely companions” is a tired cliche by this point, but that doesn’t make it any less true to say that on the surface, the two had very little in common. Raymond was a young twentysomething raised on an inner-city housing estate and serving a prison sentence at HMP Brixton. Meanwhile Rylance was twice his age, a successful professional actor, and artistic director of Shakespeare’s Globe. Nevertheless that meeting, at a Shakespeare workshop in the prison, turned into a professional connection, which soon evolved into a solid friendship. Continue reading...

data.title: Filip Hrgovic stuns Britain’s Moses Itauma to claim IBF world heavyweight title
data.description: 21-year-old Itauma stopped after ninth-round rally 34-year-old Hrgovic is first Croat to win such a title Cameron outpoints Mayer to unify 154lb titles Moses Itauma’s hopes of becoming the second-youngest world heavyweight champion in history lay in ruins after the extraordinarily tough and resilient Filip Hrgovic stopped him in the ninth round of their IBF title fight. Yet, until the latter stages of round eight, the sheer speed and dextrous power of the Briton had dominated the contest, with the Croat being dropped in the second and caught again and again by jolting combinations. The fight changed course when Itauma’s stamina suddenly dipped and he began to weave in woozy fatigue as Hrgovic fought back with granite-like determination. Itauma could not withstand the dark storm rolling over him in the ninth and he sank back against the ropes as Hrgovic opened up with renewed conviction. Just as the referee stepped in to stop the fight, Ben Davison, Itauma’s trainer, also sent a white towel sailing sadly over the listing ropes to save his man from a knockout. Continue reading...

data.title: Erasmus tricks and Kolisi magic inspire Springboks to level series with All Blacks
data.description: Second Test: South Africa 33-26 New Zealand Head coach changes front-row just before start The Boks are back. Level at one apiece in the series after a return to what they do best. Blending power and directness, blood and thunder, to edge far enough ahead of New Zealand and withstand a gutsy comeback from the All Blacks. Throw in some brazen mischief from Rassie Erasmus, who swapped his entire front-row just an hour before kick-off, and this was much closer to a trademark Springboks performance after they were unrecognisable a week ago. South Africa were far from flawless but constantly ferocious. It was not a knockout blow – not least given how the All Blacks finished the match – but it was some counterpunch after last week’s humbling. The third Test is scheduled for Johannesburg but they may consider relocating to Manila. Continue reading...

data.title: Lavish spending fails to fix Tottenham’s big issue – the lack of soul and spine | Jonathan Liew
data.description: It might be too early to push the panic button but Roberto De Zerbi faces a huge task if he is to turn Spurs around Time for Tottenham to start panicking? This is, of course, a subtle trick question. Tottenham is one of those clubs that never actually stops panicking. They panic when they concede and they panic when they score. They panic when they have the ball and they panic when someone else does. They have a coach in Roberto De Zerbi whose face evokes a state of permanent alarm, the expression of a man perpetually having a toilet door opened on him. One year they even managed to panic their way to the Europa League. For the ever-rattled Spurs fan, this club is less a treasured devotion and more a lifelong haunting, broken up by occasional panic substitutions. You could intuit that sense of encrusted resignation pretty much from the moment Anthony Elanga’s improvised shot kissed the post and trickled over the line to give Newcastle the lead. Since beating Aston Villa 4-1 in late 2024, Tottenham have gone behind 44 times in all competitions and come back to win precisely zero of them. There is something innate and endemic here, a chronic case of Long Tottenham for which – despite the new coach, the new leadership structure and more than a third of a billion pounds in transfer fees – there remains no proven cure. Yoane Wissa’s clincher was of zero surprise to anyone. Continue reading...

data.title: Trump’s ‘economic D-day’ against Iran risks driving the stakes even higher | Sina Toossi
data.description: As with its approach to Hormuz, the US has mistaken applying pressure for an actual strategy. But Tehran has chips of its own to play Donald Trump has found a new way to promise victory over Iran. After months of war have failed to force Iran’s capitulation or collapse, his administration has unveiled what the US Treasury secretary, Scott Bessent, calls Operation Economic Outcast: an effort to cut it off from what remains of the global economy and threaten foreign governments, banks and companies with sanctions if they continue doing business with Tehran. There is no question that Iran is vulnerable. Its economy has been battered by years of sanctions, war and a months-long US naval blockade. Iranian officials acknowledge that oil exports and access to foreign currency have been severely constrained. Ordinary Iranians are already enduring high inflation, currency depreciation and worsening living standards. Further economic strangulation will inflict significant additional hardship. Sina Toossi is a senior non-resident fellow at the Center for International Policy, where his work focuses on US-Iran relations, US policy toward the Middle East and nuclear issues Continue reading...

data.title: The rebranding of ‘Lake America’ is Trump’s desperate attempt to distract us | Arwa Mahdawi
data.description: Ignore Iran, the Epstein files, and your wallet – not to mention Trump’s plummeting approval ratings Don’t mention the war! Or the economy, for that matter. Or the Epstein files. Or Natalie Harp. Or “affordability”, which, as Donald Trump recently said at a rally, is a word that was “never used” by the media before he took office. Best not to talk about anything that affects ordinary people or embarrasses the president, really. Instead, let’s all rejoice in Trump’s latest triumph: renaming Lake Ontario, which is shared by Canada and the US, as Lake America . On Thursday, Trump signed an executive order directing federal agencies to America-fy the lake’s name on US maps and documents, which is an excellent use of time and resources. I suppose we can at least be thankful that the president, who is trying to slap his own name on everything from airports to the Kennedy Center , didn’t decree that the body of water be called Lake Trump. Arwa Mahdawi is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

data.title: Ukraine war briefing: Nuclear plant has lost power and running on generators, UN watchdog says
data.description: Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia plant has 10-day diesel supply on site; Kyiv investigates deadly attack on warehouse. What we know on day 1,649 The Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant in Ukraine has been without off-site power for more than a week and is now relying on emergency diesel generators, the UN’s nuclear watchdog says. The plant, which needs power to keep its six non-operating reactors cool, has only a 10-day diesel supply on site, the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) said on Saturday. “The availability of diesel fuel is of paramount importance whenever a nuclear power plant loses off-site power, ” said agency director general Rafael Grossi. “The current situation once again shows why reliable external power and secure supply routes are indispensable for nuclear safety and security.” The plant had been supplied with diesel on Thursday and Friday from another off-site location, the IAEA added. Zaporizhzhia lost its regular power supply “following military activity on the northern side of the Dnipro River”, the statement said. The IAEA said it was trying to negotiate a local ceasefire to allow repairs to electrical lines. The plant, in southern Ukraine, was seized by the Russian army in March 2022 and its six reactors have been shut down since that year. Germany is reportedly preparing to blame Russia for an attempted drone attack at Leipzig airport and impose sanctions on Russian entities . These workers form part of north-east England’s automotive industry, which has experienced a long line of political disruptions, from Margaret Thatcher’s efforts to attract international investment , through Brexit and now Andy Burnham’s reindustrialisation strategy . data.title: Women in UK arts feel they do not have equal opportunities for roles, says report
data.description: Exclusive: Research says sector is fixated with young talent, with most women experiencing unconscious bias or sexism Women working in the arts believe they do not have equal opportunities for roles, especially as they get older, according to a report saying that the industry is fixated with “young and emerging” talent. Nearly all (95%) women working in the arts thought gender inequality persisted, while three-quarters (75%) reported experiencing unconscious bias or sexism, according to a survey of 76 arts professionals. More than two-thirds (69%) felt that age negatively affected their career success – a figure that rose to 100% among those working in artistic rather than managerial roles. Continue reading...

data.title: Pet owners at risk of being ripped off by private equity firms as vet ownership rules change
data.description: Critics say changes by CMA will allow multinationals to obscure their ownership of vet practices Pet owners have been warned that they could be unknowingly ripped off by private equity firms who have bought local vet clinics, after the Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) removed requirements for multinational companies to disclose which practices they own. The CMA recently ran an investigation into the monopolisation of vet practices , and found that the lack of competition and transparency of ownership had led to high prices and a lack of information for customers. Pet owners were often unaware their local vet practice could be owned by an international private equity company. Continue reading...

data.title: Nasa space telescope set to launch after surviving Trump budget cuts
data.description: Searching for exoplanets and clues on planet formation, the Roman telescope will lift off Sunday morning in Florida A $4.3bn space telescope that Donald Trump tried to kill is set to lift off from Florida early on Sunday as Nasa embarks on the next stage of its quest to unlock the secrets of the universe. The Nancy Grace Roman space telescope survived two rounds of proposed White House budget cuts, and will embark on a million-mile journey into deep space from a launchpad at the Kennedy Space Center at 7.26am ET, barring late technical issues or intervention from Florida’s notoriously capricious summer weather. Continue reading...

data.title: FBI no longer banning all applicants who have had sexual encounters with sex workers
data.description: Bureau to still dismiss those with encounters within past 10 years, three or more times or while in public safety capacity The FBI is dropping a categorical hiring ban on applicants who have had sexual encounters with sex workers and will instead consider in a more holistic manner at least some candidates who have engaged in the practice in the past, according to people familiar with the matter. The move away from an automatic disqualification falls along a continuum of evolving recruitment standards within federal law enforcement and at the buttoned-up bureau, which several years ago relaxed its approach to candidates’ past marijuana use and has drawn more recent concern among some current and former agents about a perceived loosening of recruitment requirements as it seeks to replenish its ranks. Continue reading...

data.title: When Prophecy Fails review – gripping dive into a doomsday cult
data.description: Studio theatre, Edinburgh Groupwork’s physical theatre show captures the real story of a midwest mystic from the 50s and the followers she drew, in all their eerie ordinariness In the early 1950s in the American midwest, a woman known by the alias of Marian Keech awoke in the night with the urge to write. But the words that came out weren’t her own: it was the voice of her late father, she was sure. Other voices from the beyond began to use Marian as a conduit, ultimately Jesus Christ himself, which is how Keech came to be at the centre of a doomsday cult of seemingly ordinary citizens convinced the world was about to end, but that they would be rescued by aliens from the planet Clarion. It is such a good story, one that was captured in a landmark social psychology study at the time as well as the book When Prophecy Fails, that you could argue Scottish theatre company Groupwork don’t have a lot to do. But their treatment of the tale is deceptively simple in a very well-crafted show that does no more and no less than it needs to. Continue reading...

data.description: Working in a high-end restaurant was stressful and scarring. It took an accidental encounter with the TV show to help me heal – and change my attitude towards work Eight years ago, I was working as a waitress in a fine dining restaurant in the Cotswolds. The expertly crafted atmosphere had dim mood lighting, ambient music and a farm-to-table menu. I hated it. The other waiters could charm guests into purchasing expensive bottles, but I just gaped gormlessly when I struggled to recall the wine pairings. My brown leather brogues gave me blisters as I’d hobble to the kitchen to admit I’d forgotten an order in the middle of a busy dinner service. The chefs would shout and shake the ticket in my face. data.title: Kismet, London SE1: ‘The sort of beans that make you want to move to the sun’ – restaurant review
data.description: The first genuinely cool thing to have happened in Borough Market for ages A Turkish-Cypriot meyhane , which translates roughly as “wine house”, has slotted in upstairs at the Globe Tavern in Borough Market , south London. Any cab driver worth his salt will bend your ear over the fact that this is “where Bridget Jones lives”, which might be a bit confusing if you’ve booked in to eat kuzu şiş (lamb neck kebabs) and to knock back a couple of rakis with a fermented turnip juice chaser. That Bridget Jones trivia, by the way, is completely true: the upstairs space at the Globe was used as the heroine’s gaff in that famous film franchise. Now, however, when you climb the staircase up to Kismet , an old, slightly eerie and flickering TV by the restaurant entrance begins to tell a very different tale. This is chef Keiran Mustafa ’s very personal tribute to his family’s homeland and the community they built in London. Mustafa was the opening head chef at BiBi, to my mind one of the best restaurants in London , and before that he worked at industry stalwarts Chez Bruce and the Harwood Arms . Continue reading...

data.title: In the 1940s, Nevada’s six-week divorce law turned a 1,627-acre ranch into a refuge for women seeking quick divorces; now it is becoming the state’s 28th park
data.description: Transforming from a historic divorce haven into a state park, Nevada's Lower Carson Ranch now spans 1,627 acres alongside the Carson River, preserving crucial wildlife habitats. This transition marks the end of 155 years of private ownership, officially now under Nevada State Parks. While development for future public use is underway and access is limited, the community is actively participating in selecting a new name for the park.

data.title: American startup raises $180 million to drill rock over 5km deep to build world's first superhot geothermal plant at 500 °C
data.description: Quaise Energy has successfully raised $180 million for its groundbreaking superhot geothermal plant initiative. Utilizing cutting-edge microwave technology, the project vaporizes rock instead of using conventional drill bits. Collaboration with Nabors Industries will provide essential drilling expertise and equipment. The Obsidian Project, located in Oregon, is set to generate 50 MW by 2030, paving the way for a sustainable energy future.

data.title: L’Islande rejette les négociations d’adhésion à l’Union européenne

data.title: Au camping des Grands Pins de Lacanau-Océan, soixante ans d’adaptation aux défis climatiques percutés par la menace des incendies de l’été
data.description: « Trois générations de… » La famille à la tête de l’établissement cinq étoiles a toujours navigué entre l’impératif de modernisation de son offre et celui de la protection de l’environnement. L’incendie du Porge, qui a conduit à l’évacuation du camping, plonge ce modèle dans l’inconnu.

data.title: Roman, le nouveau télescope spatial de la NASA, part à la recherche de l’énergie noire et des exoplanètes
data.description: Ce télescope, qui doit s’envoler dimanche à bord d’une fusée de Cap Canaveral, en Floride, est la mission scientifique la plus ambitieuse de l’agence depuis le James-Webb, en 2021. En cinq ans, il devrait achever trois grands relevés du ciel et aider à faire progresser l’astronomie dans tous les domaines.

data.title: US Open 2026 : à l’image d’Arthur Fils, une nouvelle vague bouscule la hiérarchie au sommet d’un tennis mondial

data.title: En Cisjordanie, des colons israéliens attaquent un village palestinien
data.description: Selon des témoins, plusieurs dizaines de colons ont encerclé une maison de Qusra avant d’en être chassés par les forces de l’ordre, mais aucun n’a été interpellé. Le propriétaire de la maison assure que les occupants ont été menottés et frappés, avant d’être relâchés.

data.title: Esclerose múltipla também afeta crianças; diagnóstico e tratamento precoces levam a maior controle da doença
data.description: A esclerose múltipla (EM) é uma doença autoimune, inflamatória e crônica. É caracterizada pela presença de cicatrizes -as escleroses- ao longo do sistema nervoso. Por isso, o impulso elétrico dos neurônios não é corretamente transmitido, o que provoca sintomas como falta de equilíbrio, tontura, visão embaçada, dificuldade de raciocínio, entre outros. data.title: O joio, o trigo e as pedras fundamentais no Poder Judiciário
data.description: Há um populismo que chega ao poder atacando inequivocamente instituições . Há outro, talvez mais insidioso, que começa por torná-las indignas de serem defendidas. O método consiste em escolher uma distorção real, repeti-la à exaustão, transformando-se a exceção em regra, de modo a que essa parte, finalmente, passe a explicar o todo, diluindo a institucionalidade para não deixar pedra sobre pedra. A crítica, indispensável em qualquer democracia, deixa então de servir à correção e passa a alimentar a deslegitimação. Nenhuma instituição sobrevive incólume quando sua caricatura se torna mais conhecida que sua realidade. Leia mais (08/29/2026 - 22h00)

data.title: Anders Svensson: Skinka, penis och balkong – balle kan betyda mycket
data.description: Det är frestande att leka med flertydigheten i ordet balle. Historiskt har det betytt ett avrundat, köttigt parti av kroppen – som en skinka. Numera används det ibland som synonym för balkong, skriver Språktidningens Anders Svensson.
data.translatedTitle: Anders Svensson: Ham, penis and balcony - balls can mean a lot
data.translatedDescription: It's tempting to play with the ambiguity of the word ball. Historically, it has meant a rounded, fleshy part of the body — like a ham. Nowadays it is sometimes used as a synonym for balcony, writes Språktidningen's Anders Svensson.

data.title: Nya teorin: Det kan ligga bakom den förödande flodvågen
data.description: Nya bilder från glaciären i Nepal och Tibet sprids. De kan kasta nytt ljus över hur flodvågen uppkom. – När jag tittar på bilderna nu ser det snarare ut som att det är berget som har lossnat, säger Mats Eriksson, avdelningschef på Statens geotekniska institut.
data.translatedTitle: The new theory: It could be behind the devastating tidal wave
data.translatedDescription: New pictures from the glacier in Nepal and Tibet are spreading. They can shed new light on how the tidal wave arose. - When I look at the pictures now, it looks more like it is the rock that has come loose, says Mats Eriksson, head of department at the Norwegian Geotechnical Institute.

data.title: Här blir fotbollen en väg ur missbruk: ”Du är aldrig ensam”

data.translatedTitle: Here, football becomes a way out of addiction: "You are never alone"
data.translatedDescription: Simon gambled away half a million. Malin lived in a cooled mobile home. Then they found Gatulaget in Hittarp in Scania. For a few months, DN's Hanna Grosshög and Anders Hansson followed the team that makes people who have lived with addiction and mental illness start to dream.

data.title: Rapport: Farliga batterier dumpas i fattiga länder
data.description: Den snabba elbilsomställningen riskerar att skapa en global avfallskris. Medan rikare länder utvecklar system för återvinning av litiumjonbatterier, leder en prispress i låg- och medelinkomstländer till en farlig hantering av giftiga blybatterier, skriver Stockholm Environment Institute (SEI) i en ny rapport. – Det är rena vilda västern, säger forskaren Maria Xylia.
data.translatedTitle: Report: Dangerous batteries are dumped in poor countries
data.translatedDescription: The rapid transition to electric cars risks creating a global waste crisis. While wealthier countries are developing systems for recycling lithium-ion batteries, price pressure in low- and middle-income countries is leading to dangerous handling of toxic lead batteries, the Stockholm Environment Institute (SEI) writes in a new report. - It's pure wild west, says researcher Maria Xylia.

data.title: Jonas Gardell: ”Svaret på backlashen måste vara att vi ska böga oss”
data.description: Romansviten och tv-serien ”Torka aldrig tårar utan handskar” gav röst åt de svenskar som levde och dog i hiv-epidemin, och blev en enorm succé. Nu kommer trilogin i nyutgåva – samlad i en enda volym. Samtidigt sätts den upp som musikal. – Det här är mitt livsverk, det viktigaste jag någonsin kommer ha gjort, säger Jonas Gardell.
data.translatedTitle: Jonas Gardell: "The answer to the backlash must be that we should bow down"
data.translatedDescription: The novel suite and TV series "Never wipe tears without gloves" gave voice to the Swedes who lived and died in the HIV epidemic, and became a huge success. Now comes the trilogy in a new edition - collected in a single volume. At the same time, it is staged as a musical. - This is my life's work, the most important thing I will ever have done, says Jonas Gardell.

data.title: Åsa Beckman: Dolly Parton visste hur ömtålig relationen är mellan rivaliserande kvinnor
data.description: Mitt på dansgolvet stod Agne Fälldin. Han skulle aldrig välja mig. Men på vägen hem i bilen spelades ”Jolene” – och i det ögonblicket förstod jag att relationen mellan kvinnor kan präglas både av konkurrens och ömhet, skriver DN:s Åsa Beckman.
data.translatedTitle: Åsa Beckman: Dolly Parton knew how fragile the relationship is between rival women
data.translatedDescription: Agne Fälldin stood in the middle of the dance floor. He would never choose me. But on the way home in the car, "Jolene" was played - and at that moment I understood that the relationship between women can be characterized by both competition and tenderness, writes DN's Åsa Beckman.

data.translatedTitle: Swedish House Mafia tar Tomorrowland till Ullevi – men tappar sin edge

data.title: Kanada hånar Trump för ”Lake America”

data.translatedTitle: Erik Esbjörnsson: First Nobel Prize - now on the brink of a major war
data.translatedDescription: JOHANNESBURG. Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize just a year after taking office. Since then, conflicts have followed each other in Ethiopia and now the country is on the brink of a major war, which endangers the security of the entire region.

data.title: 29 augusti: Missa inte dagens nyheter

data.translatedTitle: August 29: Don't miss today's news
data.translatedDescription: King Hakkon gave a memorial speech to his father, the police forces a five-year-old in a viral clip and this is the limit for voting support for the Liberals - here are the news you cannot miss from the day.

data.title: Sergej Lebedev: Att göra upp listor över Rysslands offer skipar ingen rättvisa
data.description: Det ryska civilsamhället och den exilryska oppositionen har i första hand koncentrerat sig på minnet av statens offer. Men om den ryska staten inte konfronteras direkt i sin roll som mördare blir resultatet moralisk förlamning, skriver exilförfattaren Sergej Lebedev i en essä om statsförbrytarnas eviga straffrihet.
data.translatedTitle: Sergey Lebedev: Making lists of Russia's victims does not do justice
data.translatedDescription: Russian civil society and the Russian opposition in exile have primarily concentrated on the memory of the victims of the state. But if the Russian state is not confronted directly in its role as murderer, the result will be moral paralysis, writes the exiled writer Sergey Lebedev in an essay about the eternal impunity of state criminals.

data.title: DN Debatt. ”Väljarna är trötta på en integrationsdebatt utan lösningar”

Väljarna efterfrågar inte att vi blundar för problem, men de har tröttnat på generaliseringar och ett ensidigt negativt fokus, skriver Ahmed Abdirahman, Järvaveckan, och Edvin Boije, Indikator Opinion.
data.translatedTitle: DN Debate. "Voters are tired of an integration debate without solutions"
data.translatedDescription: DN DEBATE. Three out of four voters believe that politicians talk more about problems than solutions when it comes to integration. The criticism cuts right across party lines. The voters are not asking us to turn a blind eye to problems, but they are tired of generalizations and a one-sided negative focus, write Ahmed Abdirahman, Järvaveckan, and Edvin Boije, Indikator Opinion.

"Life as a gift" is about the brother Hans who died of tuberculosis and the unequally distributed happiness in the family. data.title: De hockeyploeg die nooit een finale verloor, staart voor zich uit na pijnlijke shoot-outs tegen Argentinië. ‘Nu is het even leeg’
data.description: De Nederlandse vrouwen, al sinds 2014 heersend wereldkampioen, kunnen de nederlaag in de finale tegen Argentinië moeilijk bevatten. „Ik heb zelfs in de jeugd, bij Jong Oranje, niks verloren.”
data.translatedTitle: The hockey team that never lost a final stares into space after painful shoot-outs against Argentina. 'Now it's empty for a while'
data.translatedDescription: The Dutch women, reigning world champions since 2014, find it difficult to comprehend the defeat in the final against Argentina. “I didn't lose anything even in my youth, with the Dutch Juniors.”

data.title: De excuses van het kabinet voor excessen in de jeugdzorg worden met gemengde gevoelens ontvangen – ‘Ik vond het een shitshow’
data.description: Het kabinet maakte officiële excuses voor misstanden in de gesloten jeugdzorg, waar naar schatting 20.000 jongeren te maken kregen met zaken als eenzame opsluiting, vernedering, verplichte anticonceptie en voeding onder dwang. Nog altijd verblijven jongeren in gesloten zorginstellingen. „We moeten de overgang zorgvuldig uitvoeren.”
data.translatedTitle: The government's apology for excesses in youth care is received with mixed feelings - 'I thought it was a shit show'
data.translatedDescription: The government made an official apology for abuses in the closed youth care system, where an estimated 20,000 young people were faced with issues such as solitary confinement, humiliation, mandatory contraception and force-feeding. Young people still stay in closed care institutions. “We must carry out the transition carefully.”

data.title: Hier heeft de extreemrechtse Israëlische minister Ben-Gvir zijn ideeën vandaan: het „apocalyptische gedachtegoed” van rabbijn Kahane is overal in Israël
data.description: De Israëlische minister Itamar Ben-Gvir noemde Palestijnen „geen mensen”. Zijn extremisme is sterk beïnvloed door de ideeën van rabbijn Meir Kahane. Diens invloed op de Israëlische politiek groeit, constateert hoogleraar Shaul Magid, die een boek over hem schreef.
data.translatedTitle: This is where the far-right Israeli minister Ben-Gvir got his ideas: Rabbi Kahane's "apocalyptic ideas" are everywhere in Israel
data.translatedDescription: Israeli Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir called Palestinians “not people.” His extremism is strongly influenced by the ideas of Rabbi Meir Kahane. His influence on Israeli politics is growing, notes professor Shaul Magid, who wrote a book about him.

data.title: Schoten en explosies in Niger, ‘muitende militairen’ vallen doelen aan in hoofdstad Niamey
data.description: Sinds de staatsgreep van 2023 wordt het West-Afrikaanse Niger bestuurd door een militaire junta. Een deel van de militairen keerde zich zaterdag tegen de leiders daarvan.

data.translatedDescription: Since the 2023 coup, the West African nation of Niger has been ruled by a military junta. Some of the soldiers turned against their leaders on Saturday.

data.description: Als scholier demonstreerde Steven Everts tegen Amerikaanse kruisraketten. Veertig jaar later pleit hij voor een sterker bewapend Europa. Wat gebeurde er met het wereldbeeld waarmee zijn generatie opgroeide?

data.title: Nach Vuelta-Sturz: Brüche bei Radstar Pogacar
data.description: Für den Strassenrad-Weltmeister Tadej Pogacar dürfte die Saison gelaufen sein. Er erlitt beim Sturz auf der achten Etappe der Vuelta Brüche am Schlüsselbein und am Halswirbel – und muss operiert werden.
data.translatedTitle: After the Vuelta crash: fractures at Radstar Pogacar
data.translatedDescription: The season is probably over for road cycling world champion Tadej Pogacar. He suffered fractures to his collarbone and cervical vertebra in a fall on the eighth stage of the Vuelta - and needs surgery.

data.title: Ministerium: Soldaten meutern gegen die Militärregierung im Niger
data.description: In dem bitterarmen Land rebellieren abtrünnige Soldaten gegen die Regierung. Schüsse und Explosionen erschüttern die Hauptstadt Niamey. Hat das Militär die Meuterei erfolgreich stoppen können?
data.translatedTitle: Ministry: Soldiers mutiny against the military government in Niger

data.description: Das asiatische Handelshaus wird des Betrugs verdächtigt. Nun fordert Radiant World Hunderte Millionen Dollar vom Schweizer Rohstoffriesen zurück. Am Schweizer Handels- und Finanzplatz hatte so manches Unternehmen eine Geschäftsbeziehung mit Radiant.

data.title: Erst Kursverzehnfachung, dann Korrektur: Nun könnte diese Aktie mit Bezug zu Trump neu durchstarten [premium]
data.description: Diese spekulative Aktie, von der „Presse“ vor über einem Jahr vorgestellt, hat mit ihrem Höhenflug schon einmal verblüfft. Experten meinen, dass sie es nun wieder tun und ihren Wert sogar mehr als verdreifachen könnte.
data.translatedTitle: First the price increased tenfold, then a correction: Now this stock could take off again with reference to Trump [premium]
data.translatedDescription: This speculative share, introduced by the “Presse” over a year ago, has already amazed people with its soaring heights. Experts believe it could now do it again and even more than triple its value.

data.title: Ozonloch: Hartnäckiger als bisher gedacht      [premium]
data.description: Auch wenn die Emissionen von FCKW deutlich zurückgehen, wird sich das Ozonloch nicht so bald komplett schließen. Eine neue Studie zeigt, dass natürliche Halogen-Emissionen die Erholung der Ozonschicht verzögern.
data.translatedTitle: Ozone hole: more persistent than previously thought [premium]
data.translatedDescription: Even if CFC emissions decline significantly, the ozone hole will not close completely any time soon. A new study shows that natural halogen emissions are delaying the recovery of the ozone layer.

data.title: Carlos Alcaraz und die Belastungsfrage: Wie viele Grand Slams hält sein Körper aus? [premium]
data.description: Carlos Alcaraz ist mit 23 Jahren erfolgreicher, als es Roger Federer, Rafael Nadal und Novak Djokovic im selben Alter waren. Die Frage nach neuen Rekorden ist vor allem eine der Frage der Belastbarkeit. Auch bei den US Open in New York.
data.translatedTitle: Carlos Alcaraz and the stress question: How many Grand Slams can his body withstand? [premium]
data.translatedDescription: At 23, Carlos Alcaraz is more successful than Roger Federer, Rafael Nadal and Novak Djokovic were at the same age. The question of new records is above all a question of resilience. Also at the US Open in New York.

data.title: Silvester vom Nordlicht bis zum Mittelmeer
data.description: Glanzvoller Jahreswechsel. Zwischen mediterranem Lichterglanz, alpiner Winterkulisse und arktischem Himmel führen fünf besondere Reisen stilvoll, genussvoll und voller Atmosphäre ins neue Jahr.
data.translatedTitle: New Year's Eve from the Northern Lights to the Mediterranean
data.translatedDescription: Brilliant turn of the year. Between Mediterranean lights, an Alpine winter backdrop and an Arctic sky, five special trips lead into the New Year in style, enjoyment and full of atmosphere.

data.title: „Meine Furchtlosigkeit habe ich verloren“ – Schauspielerin Sarah Frick kämpft sich durch eine schwere Lebenskrise [premium]
data.description: Sarah Frick durchlebt eine äußerst schwierige Zeit. Vor sechs Monaten starb ihre Schwester und vor wenigen Wochen – mitten während der Theaterproben – trafen die Schauspielerin zwei weitere Schicksalsschläge.
data.translatedTitle: “I have lost my fearlessness” – actress Sarah Frick fights through a serious life crisis [premium]
data.translatedDescription: Sarah Frick is going through an extremely difficult time. Her sister died six months ago and a few weeks ago - in the middle of theater rehearsals - the actress suffered two further strokes of fate.

data.title: Auch die teuerste Geige ist nur aus Holz [premium]
data.description: Im auf Deutsch irreführend „Der Klang der Stradivari“ genannten Film „Les Musiciens“ von Grégory Magne empfängt das Publikum die naiv-schlichte, aber herzerwärmende Botschaft, dass man nur unter Freunden gut musizieren kann.
data.translatedTitle: Even the most expensive violin is only made of wood [premium]
data.translatedDescription: In the film “Les Musiciens” by Grégory Magne, which is misleadingly called “The Sound of Stradivarius” in German, the audience receives the naively simple but heartwarming message that you can only make good music with friends.

data.title: „Ein echtes Dirndl ist eine Wertanlage“ [premium]
data.description: Ein Dirndl passt fast immer, sagt Trachtenunternehmerin Anna Tostmann-Grosser. Neben der „besonderen Ausstrahlung“ des Kleidungsstücks gibt es aber auch einige No-Gos. Ebenso bei der Lederhose.
data.translatedTitle: “A real dirndl is an investment” [premium]
data.translatedDescription: A dirndl almost always fits, says traditional costume entrepreneur Anna Tostmann-Grosser. In addition to the “special charisma” of the item of clothing, there are also some no-gos. Likewise with lederhosen.

data.title: Die perfekte Tomatensauce [premium]

data.translatedDescription: What does it take to make a good sugo? Lorenz Commare cooks it in his Cucina Commare according to his Sicilian grandmother's recipe.

data.description: Was ist da los, dass immer mehr junge Menschen Komplimente verteilen als seien das Flyer für den Flohmarkt am Wochenende?
data.translatedTitle: The boys still know how to give compliments [premium]
data.translatedDescription: What is going on that more and more young people are handing out compliments as if they were flyers for the weekend flea market?

data.description: Country-Superstar Dolly Parton war eine wichtige Bezugsperson ohne Angst vor dem stilistischen „Too much“. Besonders die LGBTQ-Community liebte sie – eine Stilkolumne zu ihren Ehren.
data.translatedTitle: Dolly Parton was the queen of hearts – with a rhinestone crown [premium]
data.translatedDescription: Country superstar Dolly Parton was an important reference figure without fear of the stylistic “too much”. The LGBTQ community especially loved her - a style column in her honor.

data.title: Was ein Alpbacher Stammtisch Europas Elite zu sagen hat
data.description: Europas politische, wirtschaftliche und intellektuelle Elite diskutiert im idyllischen Tiroler Bergdorf darüber, wie der Kontinent wieder stärker werden kann. Doch was halten eigentlich jene davon, die das Forum jedes Jahr direkt vor ihrer Haustür erleben? Über den Wunsch nach „mehr europäischem Selbstbewusstsein“ und „weniger Gesprächsblasen“, einen Auftrag an Forumspräsident Othmar Karas und einen Bus ohne Fahrer.
data.translatedTitle: What an Alpbach regulars' table of Europe's elite has to say
data.translatedDescription: Europe's political, economic and intellectual elite are discussing how the continent can become stronger again in the idyllic Tyrolean mountain village. But what do those who experience the forum right on their doorstep every year actually think of it? About the desire for “more European self-confidence” and “fewer conversation bubbles”, an order for forum president Othmar Karas and a bus without a driver.

data.title: Was im Wiener Sommer nicht fehlen darf
data.translatedTitle: What should not be missing in the Viennese summer

data.title: Wie geht das Gehirn mit mehreren Sprachen um? [premium]
data.description: Wer zwei, drei oder mehr Sprachen spricht, muss in Sekundenbruchteilen Wörter erkennen und verstehen. Wie halten wir Sprachen auseinander?
data.translatedTitle: How does the brain deal with multiple languages? [premium]
data.translatedDescription: Anyone who speaks two, three or more languages ​​has to recognize and understand words in a split second. How do we tell languages ​​apart?

data.title: Islandia powiedziała „nie” Unii Europejskiej. Wyniki referendum
data.description: W przeprowadzonym w sobotę referendum Islandczycy odrzucili rządową propozycję wznowienia negocjacji akcesyjnych z Unią Europejską – podał islandzki nadawca publiczny RUV, zaznaczając, że do przeliczenia została niewielka liczba głosów.
data.translatedTitle: Iceland said "no" to the European Union. Referendum results
data.translatedDescription: In the referendum held on Saturday, Icelanders rejected the government's proposal to resume accession negotiations with the European Union, the Icelandic public broadcaster RUV reported, noting that a small number of votes remained to be counted.

data.title: Dziennikarz dostał PESEL członka spółdzielni. NSA: spółdzielnia nie uniknie kary
data.description: Naczelny Sąd Administracyjny podtrzymał decyzję Prezesa UODO w sprawie ukarania spółdzielni mieszkaniowej, która nie zgłosiła do UODO naruszenia ochrony danych osobowych jednego ze swoich członków i nie zawiadomiła go o tym naruszeniu. Chodzi o głośną sprawę sprzed trzech lat.
data.translatedTitle: The journalist received the PESEL number of a member of the cooperative. Supreme Administrative Court: the cooperative will not avoid punishment
data.translatedDescription: The Supreme Administrative Court upheld the decision of the President of the Personal Data Protection Office to punish a housing cooperative that did not report to the Personal Data Protection Office a breach of personal data protection of one of its members and did not notify him about the breach. It concerns a famous case from three years ago.

data.title: Najdroższy znaczek świata na wystawie w Pradze. „Mona Lisa filatelistyki”.
data.description: W Pradze rozpoczęła się wystawa znaczków pocztowych, wśród których jest najdroższy i najrzadszy znaczek na świecie - One-Cent Magenta, czyli Brytyjska Gujana. Wystawa potrwa do 6 września.
data.translatedTitle: The most expensive stamp in the world at the exhibition in Prague. "The Mona Lisa of philately".
data.translatedDescription: An exhibition of postage stamps has started in Prague, including the most expensive and rarest stamp in the world - One-Cent Magenta, i.e. British Guiana. The exhibition will last until September 6.

data.title: Nie żyje Andrzej Wielowieyski
data.description: W wieku 98 lat zmarł Andrzej Wielowieyski – żołnierz Armii Krajowej, działacz katolicki, w czasach PRL opozycjonista, ekspert „Solidarności” i doradca Lecha Wałęsy, po 1989 r. senator, poseł i eurodeputowany, kawaler Orderu Orła Białego.
data.translatedTitle: Andrzej Wielowieyski is dead
data.translatedDescription: Andrzej Wielowieyski died at the age of 98 - a soldier of the Home Army, a Catholic activist, an oppositionist during the Polish People's Republic, an expert of "Solidarity" and an advisor to Lech Wałęsa, after 1989 a senator, MP and MEP, knight of the Order of the White Eagle.

data.title: W Katowicach kolej otwiera wiadukty. Ruch aut może wreszcie przyspieszyć.
data.description: Dobudowa nowych torów na trasie przez największe miasto Śląska poprawi przepustowość strategicznej dla regionu linii kolejowej, usprawni ruch pociągów i zwiększy częstotliwość ich kursowania.
data.translatedTitle: The railway opens viaducts in Katowice. Car traffic can finally speed up.
data.translatedDescription: The construction of new tracks on the route through the largest city in Silesia will improve the capacity of the strategic railway line for the region, improve train traffic and increase the frequency of trains.

data.title: Premia za wyliczenie ulgi i odzyskanie podatku to koszt uzyskania przychodów
data.description: Przedsiębiorca prowadzący działalność badawczo-rozwojową ma prawo do specjalnej podatkowej ulgi. Wynagrodzenie doradcy, które pomoże w jej rozliczeniu, można zaliczyć do firmowych kosztów.
data.translatedTitle: The premium for calculating the relief and recovering tax is a tax-deductible cost
data.translatedDescription: An entrepreneur conducting research and development activities is entitled to a special tax relief. The consultant's remuneration, which will help in settling it, can be included in the company's costs.

data.title: Samorządy zwiększają inwestycje w zeroemisyjne autobusy
data.description: W pierwszych siedmiu miesiącach 2026 r. zarejestrowano 1225 nowych autobusów miejskich, o 943 szt. więcej niż rok wcześniej. Przeszło dwie trzecie to elektrobusy i wodorowce.
data.translatedTitle: Local governments are increasing investments in zero-emission buses
data.translatedDescription: In the first seven months of 2026, 1,225 new city buses were registered, 943 more than a year earlier. More than two thirds are electric buses and hydrogen buses.

data.title: W poniedziałek w „Rzeczpospolitej” wywiad z I prezesem Sądu Najwyższego. „Maciej Berek może zostać dublerem”
data.description: W rozmowie z „Rzeczpospolitą” I prezes SN Zbigniew Kapiński zapowiada, że po wakacjach chciałby się spotkać z prezydentem i ministrem sprawiedliwości, aby przekonać ich do swojego pomysłu na uzdrowienie polskiego wymiaru sprawiedliwości.
data.translatedTitle: On Monday, in "Rzeczpospolita" there was an interview with the First President of the Supreme Court. "Maciej Berek can become an understudy"
data.translatedDescription: In an interview with "Rzeczpospolita", the first president of the Supreme Court, Zbigniew Kapiński, announces that after the holidays he would like to meet with the president and the minister of justice to convince them of his idea for healing the Polish justice system.

data.title: Modżtaba Chamenei wzywa kraje muzułmańskie do konfrontacji z „prawdziwym wrogiem”
data.description: Najwyższy przywódca duchowo-polityczny Iranu Modżtaba Chamenei wezwał kraje muzułmańskie, szczególnie leżące w Zatoce Perskiej, do zjednoczenia w walce z „prawdziwym wrogiem”, podkreślając przy tym, że podziały wśród muzułmanów służą interesom ich przeciwników – poinformowała agencja Reutera. W opublikowanym w internecie liście jako wrogów wskazał przywódców USA i Izraela.
data.translatedTitle: Mojtaba Khamenei calls on Muslim countries to confront the "real enemy"
data.translatedDescription: Iran's supreme spiritual and political leader Mojtaba Khamenei called on Muslim countries, especially those in the Persian Gulf, to unite in the fight against the "real enemy", emphasizing that divisions among Muslims serve the interests of their opponents, Reuters reported. In a letter published online, he named the leaders of the US and Israel as enemies.

data.title: W poniedziałek rusza kolejne spotkanie G20 z udziałem Polski. Będą minister finansów oraz prezes NBP
data.description: Minister finansów i gospodarki Andrzej Domański oraz prezes Narodowego Banku Polskiego Adam Glapiński w poniedziałek i wtorek mają brać udział w pracach grupy G20 w USA. Domański informował, że ma zaplanowane spotkania m.in. z przedstawicielami Japonii i Wielkiej Brytanii.
data.translatedTitle: The next G20 meeting with Poland's participation starts on Monday. There will be the Minister of Finance and the President of the National Bank of Poland
data.translatedDescription: The Minister of Finance and Economy, Andrzej Domański, and the President of the National Bank of Poland, Adam Glapiński, are to take part in the work of the G20 group in the USA on Monday and Tuesday. Domański informed that he had planned meetings, among others: with representatives of Japan and Great Britain.

data.title: Strzelanina na imprezie techno pod Zurychem. Są ofiary, rozpoczęto obławę
data.description: Jedna osoba zginęła, a pięć zostało rannych w strzelaninie na imprezie techno w szwajcarskim miasteczku Aarau niedaleko Zurychu, na północy Szwajcarii – poinformowała miejscowa policja. Trwają poszukiwania sprawcy lub sprawców.
data.translatedTitle: Shooting at a techno party near Zurich. There are victims, a manhunt has been launched
data.translatedDescription: One person was killed and five injured in a shooting at a techno party in the Swiss town of Aarau near Zurich, northern Switzerland, local police said. The search for the perpetrator or perpetrators is ongoing.

data.title: Jakub Sewerynik: Wolność słowa nie usprawiedliwia wszystkiego
data.description: Tak w sztuce, jak i w komunikacji społecznej, czasem powiedzieć mniej, znaczy więcej.
data.translatedTitle: Jakub Sewerynik: Freedom of speech does not justify everything
data.translatedDescription: Both in art and in social communication, sometimes saying less is more.

data.title: Nieoficjalnie: Szef CIA proponował w Moskwie spotkanie Trump-Putin-Zełenski
data.description: Szef CIA John Ratcliffe w Moskwie zaproponował rosyjskim władzom zorganizowanie trójstronnego spotkania z udziałem przywódców USA, Rosji i Ukrainy: Donalda Trumpa, Władimira Putina i Wołodymyra Zełenskiego – poinformował Axios.
data.translatedTitle: Unofficially: The head of the CIA proposed a Trump-Putin-Zelensky meeting in Moscow
data.translatedDescription: CIA chief John Ratcliffe in Moscow proposed to the Russian authorities to organize a trilateral meeting with the participation of the leaders of the US, Russia and Ukraine: Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Volodymyr Zelensky, Axios reported.

data.title: Agnieszka Madej: Po wyroku TK przybywa spraw o wynagrodzenie za instalacje przesyłowe
data.description: Gdy przedsiębiorca powołuje się wyłącznie na zasiedzenie pasa gruntu pod instalacje przesyłowe bez innego tytułu prawnego, coraz częściej przegrywa – mówi Agnieszka Madej, radca prawny z Kancelarii Adwokatów i Radców Prawnych Łebek, Madej i Wspólnicy.
data.translatedTitle: Agnieszka Madej: After the Constitutional Tribunal's judgment, the number of cases concerning remuneration for transmission installations is increasing
data.translatedDescription: When an entrepreneur relies solely on adverse possession of a strip of land for transmission installations without any other legal title, he or she increasingly loses, says Agnieszka Madej, a legal advisor from the Łebki, Madej i Wspólnicy Law Firm.
